As a holding company, its ability to pay dividends is further limited by restrictions on obtaining funds from subsidiaries, and there is no assurance future dividends will be declared or maintained at current levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose risks regarding their return of capital to shareholders and the discretionary nature of these programs, though AMD focuses on stock repurchases while Broadcom focuses on dividends. AMD discloses a $12 billion repurchase authorization with $4.7 billion remaining, noting that suspending or discontinuing the program could affect stock price and volatility. Broadcom discloses that it pays quarterly cash dividends but warns there is 'no assurance' they will continue, and that the Board can reduce or discontinue them at any time, which could also have a negative effect on stock price.

sentences.text: We have an approved stock repurchase program that authorizes repurchases of up to $12 billion of our common stock (Repurchase Program).
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under the Repurchase Program.
The Repurchase Program does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

Our stock repurchases could affect the trading price of our stock, the volatility of our stock price, reduce our cash reserves, and may be suspended or discontinued at any time, which may result in a decrease in our stock price.
The declaration and payment of any dividend is subject to the approval of our Board of Directors and our dividend may be discontinued or reduced at any time.
There can be no assurance that we will declare cash dividends in the future in any particular amounts, or at all.
A reduction in our cash dividend payments could have a negative effect on our stock price.

comparisons.peer_topic: Debt Obligations and Capital Return Restrictions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces risks related to its significant debt obligations ($51.0 billion in senior unsecured notes as of Dec 28, 2024) and cyclical industry nature, which pose risks to its financial condition, including potential credit rating downgrades that have already occurred in 2024. Additionally, Intel has ceased stock repurchases and suspended its quarterly dividend in Q4 2024, with additional restrictions under the CHIPS Act agreement creating uncertainty regarding future dividend payments or share repurchases.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose their capital return activities and associated risks, but with opposite execution stances. AMD actively maintains an approved repurchase program with a specific remaining balance ($4.7 billion), acknowledging risks to cash reserves and stock volatility. In contrast, Intel reports that it 'has not made repurchases of our stock' and suspended its quarterly dividend in Q4 2024, citing significant debt obligations ($51.0 billion) and restrictions as reasons for pausing returns, while also stating there is no obligation to resume repurchases.

comparisons.comparison: Micron and AMD both disclose active stock repurchase programs with specific authorization amounts and discretionary terms. AMD has authorized up to $12 billion with $4.7 billion remaining as of December 28, 2024. Micron has authorized up to $10 billion, with $300 million spent in 2024. Both companies explicitly state that the authorization does not obligate them to repurchase any specific amount, that programs may fluctuate based on cash flows and priorities, and that any pause or termination could negatively impact stock price and increase volatility.

sentences.text: We have an approved stock repurchase program that authorizes repurchases of up to $12 billion of our common stock (Repurchase Program).
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under the Repurchase Program.
The Repurchase Program does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

Our stock repurchases could affect the trading price of our stock, the volatility of our stock price, reduce our cash reserves, and may be suspended or discontinued at any time, which may result in a decrease in our stock price.

The amount, frequency, and execution of our share repurchases pursuant to our share repurchase authorization may fluctuate based on our operating results, cash flows, and priorities for the use of cash for other purposes.

The repurchase authorization could affect the trading price of our stock and increase volatility, and any announcement of a pause in, or termination of, this program may result in a decrease in the trading price of our stock.
